subject: Anodyne Health - mini trial onramp & integration readout
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tim Reynolds <tim@anodynehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Anodyne Health mini trial onramp — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Tim / Lisa —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the mini trial (2-week onramp) moving: 

Summary of what we agreed
- Scope: 2-week trial focused on document classification + redaction in the claims intake flow (sample rate: ~500 requests/day).
- Success criteria (provisional):
  - Classification accuracy >= 92% on your verification set (we'll provide a small evaluation harness).
  - End-to-end latency (95th) <= 300ms for single-turn API calls.
  - No PII leakage on streaming/tool-calling scenarios — security sign-off required.

Technical asks / integration plan high-level
1) SDK vs direct API: You said engineering prefers a lightweight Node SDK integration — we'll provide the streaming + tokenized SDK snippets and an integration checklist.
2) API routes: use /v1/generate for classification + /v1/streams for any streaming redaction preview. We'll also supply a sample wrapper for server-side tool-calling to your redaction service.
3) KV/prefix caching: we'll suggest a 30-minute KV cache for repeated templates to reduce token cost during the trial.
4) Data handling: by default logs are retained for 30 days for troubleshooting; we can change retention per your policy (security contact required).

Owners & timeline
- Redwood: Marissa (commercial lead) — overall POC owner; Karthik (technical lead) — SDK/API handoff and tech syncs; Ben (CS lead) — acceptance and evaluation coordination.
- Anodyne: Tim (product) — POC owner; Lisa (eng) — integration lead; security@anodynehealth.com — security review.

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Redwood to share: POC requirements doc + SDK integration checklist (attached).
- Anodyne to confirm: test dataset delivery and security contact for SOC2 evidence.
- Schedule: Tech kickoff (30m) — proposed Tue 6/5 10am PT.

Attachments: anodyne_poc_requirements.docx (POC scope & eval harness), sdk_integration_checklist.md (integration tasks + sample calls)

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the kickoff and loop in our infra on the day-of.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

- Dataset: We can deliver a 1,000-record verification set by EOD Monday (6/4). Files will be anonymized but will retain structure for redaction testing.
- Security: please send any SOC2 and encryption-at-rest docs to security@anodynehealth.com (they will run a quick checklist).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@anodynehealth.com>, Tim Reynolds <tim@anodynehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anodyne Health mini trial onramp — technical plan and API routes

Hi Tim / Lisa —

Following up with a concise technical implementation plan so your engineers have a clear path at kickoff: 

1) Authentication & tokens- We recommend server-side API keys scoped to the trial workspace; use short-lived session tokens for any client-side preview streaming.

2) Routes and payloads- /v1/generate — standard single-turn JSON payload: {"model": "rwd-infer-base-1", "prompt": "<doc>", "max_tokens": 256} — response includes classification label + confidence. - /v1/streams — WebSocket/HTTP streaming for redaction previews: streaming frames include partial redaction candidates and offsets to allow incremental UI masking.

3) Tool-calling pattern- For on-the-fly redaction: Redwood performs a tool call to your redaction microservice (POST /internal/redact) with the text + metadata. We’ll provide a sample middleware that retries idempotently and logs request ids for traceability.

4) SDKs and examples- Attached checklist has Node/Go snippets. The Node SDK handler exposes: createSession(), streamPreview(), callTool(). You’ll need to add a thin wrapper to translate your document schema to the prompt template we send (we included an example).

5) Observability & acceptance hooks- We’ll emit trace ids for each request and pre-built acceptance metrics (accuracy vs gold set, per-route latency histograms). During the trial we’ll enable debug logging for your workspace only.

Risk notes
- PII leakage: please ensure the redaction microservice is reachable over mTLS; we can mute logging if required.
- Throughput: 500 req/day is trivial; if spike testing is needed we’ll coordinate a short load window.

I can present this at the kickoff and walk through the sample code. If you want, I’ll also open a temporary sandbox on our side and provision keys so Lisa can try the SDK right after the call.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Hi Tim / Lisa —

Couple quick operational items from the CS side to make acceptance smooth: 
- Acceptance owner (Anodyne): Lisa — owns dataset delivery and run of the verification harness.
- Acceptance owner (Redwood): Ben — runs evaluation, posts results to shared Drive folder and flags regressions.
- Evaluation cadence: we’ll run a mid-trial check on day 7 and a final run day 14.
- Escalation: if accuracy falls >5% below target, we pause and run a joint debug session.

Marissa — can you confirm the calendar invite for Tue 6/5 10am PT?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
